The config effect is unambiguous: sigma2_B of factor-model residuals = 0.0243 vs within-run-shuffle null 97.5th pct 0.0069, permutation p=0.002; split-half same-config residual correlation across runs r=0.133 [0.073, 0.210].

findings.claim: Prediction ceiling: any config-based predictor of run-demeaned success tops out at R2 ~ 0.22; the current factor model achieves 0.119, so unmeasured config properties carry roughly AS MUCH signal again as height+width+location+style+category combined. Only ~12% of currently-unexplained variance is targetable (0.0243/0.2066); the other ~88% is rollout stochasticity plus checkpoint-x-config interaction (repeats span different checkpoints, so 10.3% is a lower bound on fixed-policy determinism).
findings.evidence: Ceiling = (factors + sigma2_B_resid)/total = (0.0279+0.0243)/0.2345 from ixr_repeatability.py; caveat noted because 27/28 runs are pi0-family variants, cross-checkpoint repeats absorb config-x-checkpoint variance into the stochastic bucket.

findings.claim: Configs are mostly stochastic but with a real deterministic tail: among 1178 repeated configs, 28% NEVER succeed across runs, 16% always succeed, 55% mixed; failure MODE also repeats (modal failure-phase agreement 0.926 among configs with >=2 failures vs 0.811 chance from the marginal phase distribution).
findings.evidence: phat distribution and phase-agreement computation in ixr_addendum_out.txt; never-succeed configs across 2+ independent checkpoints are candidate hard-config targets for data prescription.

result.conclusion: The failure landscape is ADDITIVE, not a compounding weak pocket: tall x rim, tall x hard-style, and rim x hard-style penalties combine at-or-below additively (tall x rim is +5pp sub-additive on the probability scale, best described as independent penalties on the log-odds scale), and interaction terms give exactly zero held-out-run R2/AUC gain — so targeting should treat height, rim placement, and style as independent axes rather than hunting for a joint worst-cell. On the unexplained 88% of variance: exploiting the 1178 eval configs repeated across runs, a run-demeaned variance split gives factors 11.9% / config-idiosyncratic 10.3% (permutation p=0.002) / stochastic 77.8%. Practically: (a) the deterministic-given-config prediction ceiling is R2~0.22, double what the factor model achieves, meaning unmeasured per-config properties (instance geometry details, clutter, exact pose) carry as much signal as all modeled factors combined; (b) ~28% of repeated configs never succeed under any checkpoint — a concrete, enumerable hard-config set for data prescription; (c) the remaining ~78% is rollout noise (plus checkpoint-x-config variation) and is not targetable by any config-level selection. object_split is constant and uninformative.

verdicts.corrected: Confirmed as stated on the probability scale: contrast +0.050 (run-stratified bootstrap CI [+0.005,+0.096], FL permutation p=0.062; cells 3539/1266/1721/586; demeaned means +0.125/-0.077/-0.112/-0.263 vs additive -0.313; rim>0.75 contrast +0.139). verdicts.claim: The tall and rim penalties combine almost exactly additively in LOG-ODDS (independent-obstacle model): observed tall+rim raw SR 0.140 vs log-odds-additive prediction 0.151, vs probability-additive 0.085 and multiplicative 0.196. The worst pocket is just the sum of marginal penalties on the logit scale — no compounding weak region.
verdicts.reasoning: Independently recomputed from pooled_episodes.csv (tall = obj_height>0.15, rim = max(|obj_x_rel|,|obj_y_rel|)>0.65, matching ixr_interactions.py). Raw cells reproduce exactly: 0.621 (n=3539) / 0.408 (n=1266) / 0.298 (n=1721) / 0.1399 (n=586); predictions for the tall+rim cell: prob-additive 0.085 (err 5.51pp), multiplicative 0.196 (err 5.57pp), log-odds-additive 0.151 (err 1.14pp) — claimed numbers verified to the decimal. Adversarial controls all fail to refute: (1) Run confounding is severe in the raw table (corr between run SR and fraction of episodes in the tall+rim cell = −0.795; low-SR stratified runs oversample the worst cell 3-4x), but a 28-run fixed-effect logistic gives tall:rim interaction −0.105 with config-cluster-robust SE 0.175 (z=−0.60), i.e., log-odds additivity holds WITHIN runs too. (2) Config pseudo-replication: cluster bootstrap over 3349 unique configs gives pooled logit interaction −0.092, 95% CI [−0.47, +0.25], includes 0. (3) Per-run logit interactions (25 informative runs) precision-weighted mean −0.034 (SE 0.15). (4) Run-stratified Freedman-Lane permutation of the interaction: p=0.556. (5) Scale horse-race with run FE: prob-scale interaction +5.2pp (z=+1.74), multiplicative-scale −0.337 (z=−2.56, significantly rejected), logit −0.105 (z=−0.60) — log-odds is the only scale consistent with zero interaction. (6) Threshold sensitivity: across 12 (height,rim) cutoff pairs the run-FE logit interaction spans −0.38 to +0.31, all |z|<=1.68 with mixed signs — no cherry-picked threshold. Caveat: n11=586 gives a wide interaction CI (±~0.34 logits ≈ ±4pp on p11), so 'almost exactly additive' is a point-estimate statement and modest compounding is not excluded; the small residual (0.140 observed vs 0.151 predicted) actually leans slightly toward compounding. But direction and magnitude reproduce, and the no-significant-compounding conclusion survives every control.
verdicts.corrected: Sharpened statement: tall and rim penalties are statistically consistent with exact additivity on the logit scale — pooled interaction −0.09 logits (config-cluster 95% CI [−0.47, +0.25]); run-fixed-effect interaction −0.105 (cluster-robust z=−0.60, run-stratified permutation p=0.56); observed tall+rim SR 0.140 vs log-odds-additive 0.151 (1.1pp), while probability-additive (0.085) and multiplicative (0.196, z=−2.56 rejected) both miss by ~5.5pp. Note the raw 2x2 itself is run-confounded (low-SR runs oversample the tall+rim cell, corr −0.795), so the within-run fixed-effect result, not the raw table, is the load-bearing evidence; also, with n11=586 the CI permits modest compounding (down to ~−0.45 logits), so 'no compounding' means 'no detectable compounding'.

Robot base probe (5 layouts x 2 resets, all 4 sink yaws) shows the base spawns laterally CENTERED on the sink (offset -0.11..+0.11m vs region offset ±0.56m), so this is policy/embodiment chirality (arm kinematics or camera viewpoint), not spawn asymmetry.

findings.claim: REINTERPRETATION OF THE ESTABLISHED RIM RESULT: the 'radial rim penalty max(|x_rel|,|y_rel|)>0.65' is 100% the outer (far-from-sink) end of the along-counter axis. The depth coordinate |o| NEVER exceeds 0.65 (max 0.58, each region is a narrow depth band), so I(rim>0.65) == I(|s|>0.65) with agreement exactly 1.0000 (identical FE coefficient -0.201). The gradient is monotone, not an edge effect: run x layout-demeaned success falls from +0.09 at the sink-adjacent inner edge to -0.13 at s_in 0.8-1.0 (-0.30 at |s|=0.85); joint FE regression gives s_in -0.352 (se 0.028) vs depth o_in -0.022 (se 0.027). 'No directional gradient' remains true only laterally (left vs right); sink-relative distance along the counter is strongly directional.
findings.evidence: side_05_config_and_rim.py output: agreement 1.0000, binned |s| and s_in curves, joint FE; side_fig.png right panel; per-layout corr(|s|, no-grasp start sink-dist) median +0.29 validates |s| as along-counter distance from sink.

findings.claim: The far-from-sink penalty is grasp-phase mediated (approach, not transport): run-demeaned grasp rate falls monotonically from +0.077 (|s|<0.45) to -0.228 (|s|>0.75), matching the success drop (-0.230), while the failure-mode mix stays ~86-92% fail_no_grasp in every |s| bin. Since the robot parks centered at the sink, far-along-counter objects require a longer lateral base/arm reach BEFORE grasping.
findings.evidence: side_06_final.py failure-phase table and run-demeaned grasp/success by |s| bin.

findings.claim: The side factor is orthogonal to within-region position effects: the unsigned side statistic is unchanged after residualizing quad(x_rel,y_rel)+rim (0.0889 -> 0.0893, ratio 1.01), and conversely the rim coefficient moves only -0.2012 -> -0.1967 when adding run x layout x side fixed effects. The side coin flip explains essentially none of the rim/location effect (they are different axes of the same sink-centered geometry).

findings.claim: The signed left-advantage is established only for the pi0 family: 5621/5704 clear-layout episodes are pi0-variant runs (signed R-L -0.0397, p=0.018); the GR00T subset (n=83) is uninformative (+0.098, p=0.55). No cross-policy universality claim possible from this pool.

result.conclusion: The left/right-of-sink coin flip is real and fully recoverable from the data (41/50 layouts cleanly bimodal; side = sign of one rel coordinate; regions flank the sink at lateral ±0.56m). Its systematic content is almost entirely a single universal asymmetry: objects placed on the robot's-right side of the sink succeed ~4pp less (config-level p=0.004-0.018), which cannot be spawn geometry because the mobile base parks laterally centered on the sink - pointing to policy/embodiment chirality in the pi0 family. Layout-idiosyncratic side effects beyond this common shift are weak (p=0.034 marginal, residual SD ~0.05); the naive episode-level test that ignores config repetition across runs overstates them badly (p=0.0026 vs correct config-level p=0.32) - a caution applicable to any analysis of this pooled CSV. The biggest yield is a reinterpretation of the established location effect: the 'radial rim penalty' is exactly the far-from-sink end of the along-counter axis (I(rim>0.65)==I(|s|>0.65), agreement 1.0000; depth never reaches the threshold), and it is a monotone distance-from-sink gradient (+0.09 inner edge to -0.30 outer, FE slope -0.35 vs -0.02 for depth) mediated by the grasp/approach phase, not transport. For data prescription this means: prescribe demos at large along-counter distance from the sink (both sides, slight oversampling of the robot's-right side), rather than treating 'rim' as an undirected radial band.

verdicts.corrected: Only trivial refinements: my episode-level p was 0.0020 (vs claimed 0.0026 — both ~13/5000-level Monte Carlo agreement); config-level p 0.30-0.32 across seeds; MoM true SD 0.032 config-level vs 0.080 episode-level; ICC within repeated configs 0.26 (excess over layout-shuffle null 0.07).

verdicts.claim: There IS a systematic signed side effect: the region on the sink's +x side (the robot's RIGHT when facing the sink, since the base spawns on the sink-frame -y side) succeeds ~3.9pp LESS than the left region, consistent across layouts (right better in only 17/41). Config-level permutation p=0.018 on raw run-demeaned success, p=0.0038 after residualizing category+quadratic-position effects; episode-level p=0.005. Robot base probe (5 layouts x 2 resets, all 4 sink yaws) shows the base spawns laterally CENTERED on the sink (offset -0.11..+0.11m vs region offset ±0.56m), so this is policy/embodiment chirality (arm kinematics or camera viewpoint), not spawn asymmetry.
verdicts.reasoning: Independently recomputed from pooled_episodes.csv with a from-scratch pipeline: side defined directly as sign of the sink-frame lateral coordinate (rotating obj_x_abs/obj_y_abs by the probed sink pos/yaw), not the claimed cluster labels; probe geometry cross-validated against the CSV's own rel-coords (|corr|~0.99 per layout, lateral bimodal at +/-0.57 m, exactly 41/50 layouts two-sided). With run-demeaned success, config-level aggregation (configs never mix sides; 3349 configs), harmonic per-layout weighting and within-layout permutation (10k perms, fresh seed): signed R-L = -0.0394 raw p=0.0175 (claim -0.0394, p=0.0184); own residualization (category + quadratic in sink-frame |s| and depth, a stricter distance control than the claimed x_rel/y_rel quad) gives -0.0390 p=0.0054 (claim -0.0391 p=0.0038); episode-level (permute within run x layout) -0.0394 p=0.0039 (claim 0.005); right better in 17/41 layouts (matches). Adversarial checks all fail to refute: covariate balance R-L is null (|s| p=0.49, depth p=0.43, obj height/width p=0.65/0.35, category chi2 p=0.13; composition-expected dm effects <=0.0035, an order of magnitude too small); the effect is negative within 21/28 runs (per-run t-test p=0.0076, so not run-confounding or config-repetition pseudo-replication; the lone GR00T run is also negative, rest pi0); leave-one-layout-out and leave-one-run-out stay negative throughout (-0.045..-0.032); conservative layout-as-unit tests remain significant (t p=0.0177, Wilcoxon p=0.0348). Rerunning the robot-base probe myself (different seed, 3 resets/layout, layouts 56/40/20/44/12) reproduces the spawn geometry: mobilebase0_base at sink-frame lateral -0.135..+0.148 m, depth -0.45..-0.54 m, i.e. laterally centered on the -y (front) side, ~4x smaller than the +/-0.57 m region offset; frame handedness confirms sink +x = robot's right when facing the sink. Direction, magnitude, p-values, layout count, and the spawn-symmetry mechanism check all reproduce.
verdicts.corrected: Minor corrections/caveats (do not change the verdict): (1) The claimed probe layouts 56/40/15/20/33 cover only 3 distinct sink-yaw classes (pi, -pi/2, +pi/2), not "all 4" - yaw 0 was missing; my rerun added yaw-0 layouts 44 and 12 and the base is centered there too, so the conclusion survives. (2) Base lateral spawn jitter is -0.135..+0.148 m over 3 resets/layout (slightly wider than the claimed -0.11..+0.11), still far below the +/-0.57 m region offset. (3) "Consistent across layouts" is generous phrasing: 17/41 right-better is itself unremarkable (binomial p~0.35); the effect is a modest weighted average, though it does survive a conservative layout-as-unit t-test (p=0.0177). (4) My stricter sink-frame residualization gives p=0.0054 rather than 0.0038, and my episode-level p is 0.0039 rather than 0.005 - same conclusions. (5) Raw uncontrolled right-left success difference is -3.25pp; the -3.9pp figure is the layout-weighted run-demeaned estimate.

findings.claim: Episode horizon is 600 steps and timeout censoring is real but small: extending the horizon would rescue only ~2.6% of failures (~+1.4pp overall success). Failures are NOT hidden slow successes.
findings.evidence: Global max steps_to_success=600, per-run maxima converge to 596-600 as n grows (nearmiss_01). Success hazard per 60-step window peaks at 0.202 (240-300 steps) and decays to 0.026 in the final window (540-600]; applying that last-window hazard to the 3759 still-running failures rescues ~98 episodes. Successes are not bunched at the limit: 1.3% finish in the last 5% of horizon, and density declines through the tail (101 in (0.9H,H] vs 115 in (0.8H,0.9H]). Caveat: the groot_PickPlaceCounterToSink run (n=100, 56% success) records no steps_to_success at all and is excluded from all steps analyses.

findings.claim: Fine-grained failure taxonomy (n=3803 failures): never_touched (max_lift<5mm) 1907 = 50.1%; nudged (0.5-2cm) 1116 = 29.3%; partial-lift/fumble (2-5cm) 353 = 9.3%; grasped-but-stalled far (min_sink_dist>0.3m) 201 = 5.3%; grasped-carried-near (0.15-0.3m) 146 = 3.8%; reached-sink-no-place 80 = 2.1%. True near-misses are rare: only 1.5% of failures got the object within 10cm of the sink, 4.4% within 20cm.
findings.evidence: nearmiss_02 counts; success min_sink_dist median 0.112/p90 0.275 calibrates 'at sink'. Important caveat: failure_phase labels are threshold-derived from these same variables (fail_no_grasp caps at max_lift=0.050 exactly; grasped_no_transport min_sink_dist floor=0.15; reached_sink max=0.20), so phases and continuous measures are definitionally coupled; the refinement splits WITHIN phases. ~89% of failure mass is at/before grasp — the recoverable near-miss pool is tiny, so progress-relabeling or place-stage fixes cannot move headline success much.

findings.claim: Height predicts DEPTH of failure, and the mechanism dissociates from rim: tall-object (>21cm) failures are contact-then-fumble (MORE likely to be touched but not grasped), while rim failures are approach failures (never touched at all).
findings.evidence: Run-demeaned, run-stratified permutation (nearmiss_03/04): ordinal depth (0=never_touched..5=reached_sink) among all failures — peak-height (4-8cm) +0.21 depth units (p<2e-4), tall −0.18 (p<2e-4). Within fail_no_grasp: tall episodes have P(never_touched)=0.449 vs 0.612 (diff −9.7pp, p<2e-4) — they touch/knock the object but cannot secure it; rim episodes have P(never_touched) +7.8pp (0.623 vs 0.537, p<2e-4) and lower max_lift (−1.9mm, p<2e-4) — the arm never reaches the object. Caveat: all depth-among-failure analyses condition on failure (possible collider selection).

findings.claim: Failure depth is a replicable property of the eval config, not noise: configs that fail in multiple runs fail at correlated depths.
findings.evidence: 729 configs that failed in >=2 different runs (checkpoints); cross-run correlation of run-demeaned ordinal depth r=0.301, bootstrap 95% CI [0.216, 0.384] (nearmiss_03). Supports depth as a usable per-config progress signal for curriculum/prescription, beyond the binary outcome.

findings.claim: Rim, style, and category also manifest as SLOWER successes (difficulty continuum); height does NOT — tall objects succeed at normal speed when they succeed, so height is a discrete grasp gate rather than a continuum.
findings.evidence: Run-demeaned steps_to_success among 3253 successes (nearmiss_04/05): rim successes +27 steps (321 vs 293, ~9% slower, perm p<2e-4); style-level corr(success-effect, mean demeaned steps) r=−0.365 over 48 styles (perm p=0.018); category-level r=−0.279 over 74 categories (perm p=0.021) — harder styles/categories are slower even conditional on success. Tall>21cm: steps diff −1.1 (p=0.86); peak 4-8cm: −3.8 (p=0.20) — height flat. Relevant for reward shaping: steps/progress carries graded difficulty signal for rim/style/category but not for the height effect.

findings.claim: Style does not detectably predict failure depth — its large binary effect (SD ~0.08) does not extend to progress-within-failure; null or underpowered.
findings.evidence: corr(style success-effect, style mean demeaned ordinal depth) over 50 styles = −0.25 (perm p=0.10); with max_lift among fail_no_grasp r=+0.20 (p=0.19) — opposite signs, both ns. Permutation null SD 0.15 means only |r|>~0.3 was detectable: this is 'no evidence', not 'evidence of absence'. Combined with the significant style speed effect on successes, style plausibly acts late/diffusely (execution speed + binary outcome) rather than gating a specific progress stage.

findings.claim: The slow-success tail is descriptively enriched in weak-region factors, but individual-factor enrichment is not significant.
findings.evidence: Successes with steps>480: 22.2% rim vs 14.0% among early successes; 10.6% tall vs 6.2%; lower mean style/category effects (nearmiss_05). Run-stratified permutation on P(late|success): rim +1.8pp p=0.12, tall +2.1pp p=0.28 (nearmiss_06). Episode-level corr of a crude difficulty composite with demeaned steps = 0.116. Treat as descriptive convergence with the mean-shift speed results, not independent evidence.

findings.claim: Within the fail_no_grasp stratum, height does NOT modulate partial-lift magnitude (continuous max_lift), only contact probability.
findings.evidence: Peak-height vs rest max_lift diff +0.0005m (p=0.19), tall vs rest +0.0001m (p=0.68) among 3376 fail_no_grasp episodes (nearmiss_03). The height depth effect operates entirely through the touched/not-touched and grasped/not-grasped transitions, not through 'how high the fumble got'. Distinguishes gate-like from graded mechanisms.

result.conclusion: 'Failure' on PickPlaceCounterToSink hides almost no near-successes: the 600-step horizon censors only ~2.6% of failures (+~1.4pp potential success), and just 1.5% of failures ever brought the object within 10cm of the sink. Instead, failure mass sits at the very start of the task — 50% of all failures never move the object more than 5mm — and the established factors act through two dissociable early mechanisms: rim placements cause approach failures (never touch, +7.8pp never_touched, p<2e-4) while tall objects cause contact-then-fumble failures (touched MORE, −9.7pp never_touched, but not grasped, p<2e-4). Depth of failure is a stable config property (cross-run r=0.30) and is predicted by height (ordinal depth p<2e-4), strengthening the causal reading of the height effect. Among successes, rim (+27 steps, p<2e-4), hard styles (r=−0.37, p=0.018) and hard categories (r=−0.28, p=0.021) also produce slower successes — a graded difficulty continuum usable for progress-based data selection — whereas height shows zero speed effect, marking it as a discrete grasp gate. Practical implication for prescription: collect approach/reach demonstrations for rim regions and grasp-securing demonstrations for tall objects; place-stage data would address only ~2% of failures.

verdicts.claim: Episode horizon is 600 steps and timeout censoring is real but small: extending the horizon would rescue only ~2.6% of failures (~+1.4pp overall success). Failures are NOT hidden slow successes.
verdicts.reasoning: Independent recomputation from pooled_episodes.csv reproduces every stated number to the reported precision. Horizon: global max steps_to_success = 600 exactly, none above (1 success at 600, 6 at >=596 across 3253 recorded values), confirming H=600. Steps are recorded only for successes, and the sole run with no steps is groot_PickPlaceCounterToSink (n=100, 56% success), exactly as caveated; excluding it leaves 3253 timed successes and 3759 still-running failures (3803-44). Discrete hazard per 60-step window (successes in window / at-risk at window start, failures held in the risk set to 600): peak 0.2024 in (240,300] (claimed 0.202), final window 0.0262 (claimed 0.026), with monotone decay through the tail. Rescue = 0.0262*3759 = 98.4 episodes = 2.62% of failures = +1.38pp of 7112 (claimed ~98 / ~2.6% / ~+1.4pp). Tail non-bunching reproduces: 42/3253 = 1.29% of successes finish after step 570; 101 in (540,600] vs 115 in (480,540]; tail counts 575/236/145/115/101 decline monotonically. Adversarial checks fail to overturn: (a) run-stratified rescue (per-run last-window hazard x per-run failures) = 97.2 vs pooled 98.4 — no run confounding; runs with more failures have slightly LOWER tail hazard, so pooling errs slightly high; (b) config pseudo-replication is real (3249 unique configs, 71% of episodes are repeats, max 21x) but a config-cluster bootstrap gives rescue CI [80,118] episodes = [2.1%,3.2%] of failures = [+1.1,+1.7]pp, matching the naive binomial CI; (c) no individual large run bunches successes at the limit (max 3.6% of successes in last 5% of horizon vs 5% under uniform density). Caveats that bound scope but not the verdict: the ~2.6%/+1.4pp figure is specifically a one-window (+60 step) extension; fitted decay models cap total rescue at ~9% of failures (+4.6pp, exponential fit, infinite horizon) to ~17% (power-law, +2400 steps), so the qualitative conclusion (failures are overwhelmingly not slow successes) is robust, though a large horizon extension would rescue more than 2.6%. 'Per-run maxima converge to 596-600' is loose (5 largest runs: 597, 562, 598, 588, 593). The assumption that failures ran the full 600 steps is untestable from the CSV (no step counts for failures) but consistent with fixed-horizon eval design and the failure-phase mix (only 2.1% reached the sink).
verdicts.corrected: Refined statement: horizon H=600 confirmed (max recorded steps exactly 600, none above). Excluding groot_PickPlaceCounterToSink (n=100, 56% success, no step logging), last-window (540,600] success hazard = 0.0262 (95% config-cluster CI 0.021-0.031); one additional 60-step window would rescue ~98 of 3759 censored failures (CI 80-118) = 2.6% of failures = +1.4pp overall. Extrapolating the decaying hazard to an unbounded horizon caps total rescue at roughly 9-17% of failures (+4.6 to +9pp) depending on decay model — still a small minority, so failures are not hidden slow successes, but the 2.6% figure applies to a +60-step extension, not arbitrary horizon growth. Run-stratified rescue = 97.2 (vs pooled 98.4). Tail density of successes declines monotonically (575/236/145/115/101 per window from step 300); 1.29% of successes finish in the last 5% of the horizon.

verdicts.claim: Fine-grained failure taxonomy (n=3803 failures): never_touched (max_lift<5mm) 1907 = 50.1%; nudged (0.5-2cm) 1116 = 29.3%; partial-lift/fumble (2-5cm) 353 = 9.3%; grasped-but-stalled far (min_sink_dist>0.3m) 201 = 5.3%; grasped-carried-near (0.15-0.3m) 146 = 3.8%; reached-sink-no-place 80 = 2.1%. True near-misses are rare: only 1.5% of failures got the object within 10cm of the sink, 4.4% within 20cm.
verdicts.reasoning: Independently recomputed from pooled_episodes.csv (7112 rows, 28 runs, 3803 failures). Every headline number reproduces exactly: never_touched 1907 (50.1%), nudged 1116 (29.3%), partial-lift 353 (9.3%), stalled-far 201 (5.3%), carried-near 146 (3.8%), reached-sink-no-place 80 (2.1%); near-miss <10cm = 56 (1.5%), <20cm = 169 (4.4%); success min_sink_dist median 0.112 / p90 0.275; no-grasp share 3376/3803 = 88.8% (~89%). The definitional-coupling caveat is real: fail_no_grasp max_lift caps at 0.050 exactly and grasped_no_transport min_sink_dist floors at 0.150 exactly, so the refinement indeed splits within phases. Run-confounding does not overturn it: the unweighted mean of per-run fractions across the 28 runs (success 0.250-0.593) gives 49.3/29.4/9.7/6.1/3.7/1.8 — nearly identical to pooled — and the at/before-grasp share is 78-98% in every individual run while per-run near-miss(<20cm) never exceeds 8.7%, so the "tiny recoverable near-miss pool" conclusion is robust to stratification; config repetition (up to 21x) only affects inferential SEs, not this descriptive composition. Three minor issues, none material: (1) the bins actually use <= edges, not strict < ("max_lift<5mm" is really <=5mm; strict < gives 1784/1220/372 = 46.9/32.1/9.8%, same conclusion); (2) the "far >0.3m" count of 201 silently includes 9 grasped_no_transport episodes with MISSING min_sink_dist (pure >0.3m gives 192 = 5.0%); (3) the caveat's "reached_sink max=0.20" is wrong — the actual reached_sink min_sink_dist max is 0.149, i.e. the phase threshold is 0.15, not 0.20.
verdicts.corrected: Corrections to the claim's fine print only (headline numbers all verified exact): bins use inclusive upper edges — never_touched is max_lift<=5mm (strict <5mm would give 1784 = 46.9%; nudged 1220 = 32.1%; partial 372 = 9.8%); "stalled far" 201 = 192 with min_sink_dist>0.3m plus 9 with missing min_sink_dist (pure >0.3m: 5.0%); the reached_sink phase threshold is min_sink_dist<0.15m (observed max 0.149), not 0.20 as stated in the caveat. Run-stratified (unweighted mean over 28 runs) composition: 49.3/29.4/9.7/6.1/3.7/1.8%, confirming pooled figures are not run-weighting artifacts.

verdicts.claim: Height predicts DEPTH of failure, and the mechanism dissociates from rim: tall-object (>21cm) failures are contact-then-fumble (MORE likely to be touched but not grasped), while rim failures are approach failures (never touched at all).
verdicts.reasoning: Independent recomputation (own code, own seed, 20000 within-run permutations) reproduces every quoted number to the stated precision: ordinal depth among all 3803 failures — peak 4-8cm +0.2056 (claimed +0.21, p=5e-5), tall >21cm −0.1777 (claimed −0.18, p=5e-5); within fail_no_grasp (n=3376) — tall P(never_touched) raw 0.449 vs 0.612 with run-demeaned diff −0.0972 (claimed −9.7pp, p<=2e-4), rim P(never) 0.623 vs 0.537, demeaned +0.0777 (claimed +7.8pp, p=5e-5), rim max_lift −1.88mm (claimed −1.9mm, p=5e-5). The dissociation is real: rim has NO effect on ordinal depth overall (−0.04, p=0.31) but strongly raises never-touched, while tall raises touched-not-grasped. Adversarial checks passed: (1) run confounding is severe (per-run tall fraction 0.00-0.39, anticorrelated with run success 0.25-0.59) but stratification handles it — effects replicate with the same sign when re-demeaned separately within standard-eval runs (never~tall −0.174, depth~tall −0.189, never~rim +0.092) and within targeted strat/balcat runs (−0.092/−0.219/+0.062), ruling out hard-list-selection artifacts; (2) config-repetition pseudo-replication (3349 unique configs, up to 21 repeats; tall/peak/rim constant within config) — cluster bootstrap over configs keeps all five effects at p<=0.005; (3) rim effects survive even category-level clustering (p<1e-3); (4) lift-threshold sensitivity: tall-touch effect holds at 3/5/10mm cuts; (5) all p~5e-5 trivially survive multiple comparisons; (6) collider concern is mitigated by unconditional rates: tall raises P(fail&touched-no-grasp) 0.158->0.438 (+18.6pp demeaned) vs P(fail&never-touched) 0.250->0.356 (+7.3pp), so the touched mode genuinely dominates the tall failure excess. Caveats that stop short of refutation but should temper the mechanism language: the tall effect is category-concentrated and bimodal — pitcher/cheese_grater/jar/reamer/blender_jug (615/972 = 63% of tall no-grasp failures, never=0.09-0.34) carry it, while juice/spray/wine (37%, never=0.81-0.89) show the OPPOSITE approach-failure pattern; under category-level cluster bootstrap the tall effects lose significance (p=0.20 depth, p=0.50 never) and leave-one-out dropping pitcher alone shrinks never~tall to −0.007; within-category instance height shows no depth signal (r=−0.006, ns) and only weak never signal (r=−0.057, p=0.001), so "height" is largely a proxy for tall-category identity; at a 2cm lift threshold the tall effect reverses (+4.7pp), i.e. tall objects get nudged past 5mm (knock/tip physics) but rarely achieve >2cm partial lifts — consistent with "touch/knock but cannot secure" yet meaning "touched" partly reflects easy knock-over of tall objects; 50 episodes with NaN obj_height fall silently into the "rest" group (negligible). Scripts: av_main_recompute.py, av_cluster_checks.py, av_hetero.py, av_tall_detail.py, av_sensitivity.py in /data/xinyua11/tmp/factor_analysis_scratch/.
verdicts.corrected: All quoted statistics reproduce exactly (peak +0.206 depth, tall −0.178, tall P(never) 0.449 vs 0.612 / −9.7pp demeaned, rim +7.8pp / −1.9mm max_lift, all p<=2e-4) and are robust to run stratification, config-level clustering, and run-family (standard vs targeted) splits; rim-as-approach-failure is robust even at category-level clustering. Recommended refinement: the tall "contact-then-fumble" signature is a category-weighted average, not a uniform property of height — it is driven by graspable-body tall categories (pitcher, cheese_grater, jar, reamer, blender_jug: never-touched 0.09-0.34, 63% of tall no-grasp failures), whereas carton/bottle-type tall categories (juice, spray, wine: 37%) fail rim-style (never-touched 0.81-0.89); the tall effects are not significant when clustered at the category level (n=10 tall categories, boot p=0.20/0.50), instance-level height within category carries no depth signal, and "touched" for tall objects partly reflects knock/tip physics (effect reverses at a 2cm lift threshold). State the claim as "tall-category failures are on average contact-then-fumble" rather than "height causes contact-then-fumble".

findings.claim: Region-level concentration is real but only directional: in the general eval (family E), 100% of core's net overall gain over baseline (+1.3pp) is attributable to the 10 targeted categories (+9.9pp on the 13% targeted slice, -0.1pp on the other ~70 categories), and core-vs-random on targeted is +15pp; but every arm-x-targeted interaction is non-significant (paired-config permutation p=0.40-0.41, DD +10 to +14pp with CI ~ +/-23pp; minimal detectable DD ~34pp at n~38 targeted episodes/arm).
findings.evidence: arms_weakcell_main.py section 0 + arms_mechanism.py section A: core-baseline DD=+10.0pp CI[-13.2,+33.6]; core-random DD=+14.0pp CI[-8.8,+37.4], paired p=0.396; decomposition shows targeted cells contribute +1.3 of +1.3pp (core-baseline) and +1.9 of +3.0pp (core-random).

findings.claim: In the better-powered all-targeted STRAT eval (n~280/arm on the targeted-10 categories), most of the weak-region lift is generic fine-tuning, not targeting: core +11.0pp over baseline (z=2.81, paired-config p=0.008) but random +8.9pp (z=2.31, paired p=0.024); core beats random by only +2.0pp (paired p=0.89). The family-E claim 'random data does not help where the policy is weak' (-5.1pp on targeted, n=39) is contradicted at 7x the sample size; the true core-over-random targeted advantage is +2-4pp (STRAT +2.0, BALCAT +3.8), not +15pp.
findings.evidence: arms_final.py STRAT overall table and arms_weakcell_main.py section 0b; STRAT SRs baseline 0.262, random 0.351, core 0.371; BALCAT targeted core 0.352 vs random 0.331 vs baseline 0.329.

findings.claim: No arm flattened the tall-object cliff (h>0.21m): in STRAT, tall SR is baseline 0.09 -> core 0.21 (best, CI[0.15,0.30]), random 0.17, and the saturation arm with ALL 610 targeted demos only 0.14 -- 3x more targeted data bought nothing on tall. The tall-vs-mid penalty actually GREW under core (-30pp -> -38pp) because 8-14cm objects gained most (0.48 -> 0.81). Pooled paired interaction over the 4 targeted-selection arms: tall DD +6.8pp, p=0.14 -- modest tall-concentration possible, large flattening (>~15pp) ruled out.
findings.evidence: arms_mechanism.py sections C/E + arms_final.py tall-penalty table + arms_weakcell_summary.png panel 1; height-bin curves show every arm retains the >21cm cliff (all arms <=0.21 in STRAT at n>=103 tall episodes/arm).

findings.claim: The rim penalty was untouched by every arm: pooled paired interaction over targeted arms DD=-0.4pp p=1.0 (STRAT, 185 rim pairs); core-baseline rim gain (+11.2pp) equals its center gain (+11.1pp) exactly. In family E the influence arm significantly WORSENED rim relative to center (DD=-19.6pp CI[-38.0,-0.4], paired p=0.054); coverage trended the same way (-16.5pp).
findings.evidence: arms_weakcell_main.py section 2 + arms_mechanism.py section C.

findings.claim: No arm shrank the hard-style gap (styles defined as bottom tercile from 6 independent base-policy runs, no circularity): all arm-x-hardstyle interactions non-significant, point estimates mostly zero-to-negative (STRAT core DD=-0.6pp; rc2 in family E trends worse on hard styles, -15.2pp CI[-31.2,+1.0]). Style variance -- the largest stable environment factor -- is completely unaddressed by category-targeted data.
findings.evidence: arms_weakcell_main.py section 3; hard styles = 17 of 49 rated styles from pi0_student_n500/eval_bal_A/B/failstates_eval etc.

findings.claim: There is NO dose-response within the core arm's allocation: correlation between demos-per-category and per-category gain (core-baseline, STRAT) is r=+0.06 (perm p=0.87). juice got the most demos (29) and gained nothing (8%->7%); canned_food (21 demos) gained +32pp; tupperware gained MORE under random (+42pp) than under core (+23pp). The per-category budget allocation -- the heart of the prescription algorithm -- does not predict where gains land.
findings.evidence: arms_mechanism.py section B, per-category table for the 10 targeted categories.

findings.claim: The mechanism of gains that did occur is grasp-phase: core cut fail_no_grasp from 68.5% to 59.3% of episodes overall and 89.3% to 76.7% on tall objects (STRAT), consistent with the established grasp-only weak region; but tall failures remain absolute never-lift failures in every arm (mean max_lift 0.008-0.013m among tall failures, no partial-progress shift even in saturate).
findings.evidence: arms_mechanism.py sections D/F failure-phase and progress-metric tables.

findings.claim: Verdict for the paper: the best arm (core) wins by 'lift the whole weak region without collateral damage', NOT 'fix the weak cells'. Its edge over random is (a) mostly generic fine-tuning lift shared with random, (b) a small region-level concentration bonus, and (c) coverage preservation (family E non-targeted: core -0.1pp vs coverage -8.9pp, influence -4.4pp, value -9.4pp). The deepest weak cells (h>21cm, rim, hard styles) are data-resistant to every selection strategy including 610-demo saturation -- direct quantitative support for the generation-ceiling argument that fixing them requires NEW kinds of data (human/G1), not reallocation of the existing sim pool.
findings.evidence: Synthesis of all sections; family E non-targeted gains in arms_weakcell_main.py section 0; saturate tall SR 0.14 vs core 0.21 vs baseline 0.09 in arms_mechanism.py section E.

result.conclusion: Targeted training arms lifted the weak REGION but did not fix the weak CELLS. At region level the story holds directionally: in the general eval, core's entire net gain comes from the 10 targeted categories with zero collateral loss, while spread/influence/value arms pay a non-targeted tax. But the better-powered targeted-only evals (STRAT/BALCAT, n~280 vs n~38) show (1) random fine-tuning captures ~80% of core's weak-region lift (+8.9 vs +11.0pp, core-random +2pp ns), so the celebrated +15pp core-over-random was mostly small-n noise; (2) within the weak region the lift is uniform -- the tall cliff (0.09->0.21 at best, saturate 610 demos only 0.14, penalty vs mid-height objects unchanged or larger), rim penalty (pooled DD -0.4pp), and hard-style gap (all ns, trends negative) all persist in every arm; (3) no dose-response between per-category demo allocation and per-category gain (r=0.06). Mechanism of the best arms = 'lift everything in the region and preserve the rest', achieved through the grasp phase; the geometric/style weak cells are data-resistant to any reallocation of the existing sim pool. For the prescription paper this is double-edged: it validates region-level prescription with coverage preservation as the honest headline, deflates cell-level 'fix the weakness' claims, and provides the strongest quantitative motivation yet for the generation-ceiling argument -- new data sources (human/G1), not smarter selection over the fixed pool, are required for the residual weak cells.

verdicts.claim: In the better-powered all-targeted STRAT eval (n~280/arm on the targeted-10 categories), most of the weak-region lift is generic fine-tuning, not targeting: core +11.0pp over baseline (z=2.81, paired-config p=0.008) but random +8.9pp (z=2.31, paired p=0.024); core beats random by only +2.0pp (paired p=0.89). The family-E claim 'random data does not help where the policy is weak' (-5.1pp on targeted, n=39) is contradicted at 7x the sample size; the true core-over-random targeted advantage is +2-4pp (STRAT +2.0, BALCAT +3.8), not +15pp.
verdicts.reasoning: Independently recomputed with /data/xinyua11/conda/envs/robocasa/bin/python (pandas/numpy/scipy) using different tests than the original scripts. STRAT arms (eval_strat_baseline/core/random) are 100% targeted-10 categories at n=279/280/282; SRs reproduce exactly: baseline 0.262 (73/279), random 0.351 (99/282), core 0.371 (104/280). Core-baseline +11.0pp z=+2.81, paired-config sign-flip p=0.0090 and McNemar exact p=0.0086 (claim 0.008); random-baseline +8.9pp z=+2.31, sign-flip p=0.028 / McNemar p=0.027 (claim 0.024, within MC error); core-random +2.0pp, p=0.888 (claim 0.89). Adversarial checks all fail to refute: zero within-arm config repetition (no pseudo-replication); config pairing across arms yields LARGER diffs (+13.1/+11.8pp); per-category counts are balanced and equal-category-weight SRs give the same picture (+10.7/+8.4/+2.3pp); cluster bootstrap over configs gives core-b CI [+3.4,+18.5], random-b [+1.1,+16.8] (exclude 0), core-random [-5.8,+10.2] (spans 0); independent SP runs (core 0.356 n=73 vs random 0.281 n=32 vs baseline 0.250 n=32) are consistent with a small core-random gap. Family-E contradiction reproduces: E targeted random-baseline = -5.1pp at n=39/39 (itself Fisher p=0.81, i.e. noise), STRAT is 7.2x larger and reverses it to +8.9pp; E targeted core-random = +15.0pp is the figure being debunked; BALCAT targeted raw core-random = +3.8pp. So the true core-over-random targeted advantage of +2-4pp and the 'most of the weak-region lift is generic fine-tuning' conclusion both hold. Two minor caveats (do not change direction or magnitude): the evidence line's BALCAT SRs 0.352/0.331/0.329 are the ALL-category BALCAT SRs, not the targeted subset (targeted subset is core 0.241 n=58, random 0.203 n=59, baseline 0.225 n=138; the +3.8pp gap is still correct); and random-baseline is marginal under Bonferroni x3 (corrected p~0.083), which weakens only the 'random helps' leg, not the conservative 'core~random' headline.
verdicts.corrected: All headline numbers confirmed as stated: STRAT baseline 0.262, random 0.351, core 0.371; core-baseline +11.0pp (z=2.81, paired p~0.009), random-baseline +8.9pp (z=2.31, paired p~0.027), core-random +2.0pp (paired p~0.89); E targeted random-baseline -5.1pp (n=39); core-over-random targeted advantage +2.0pp (STRAT) / +3.8pp (BALCAT), not +15pp. Corrections: (1) the cited 'BALCAT targeted core 0.352 vs random 0.331 vs baseline 0.329' are actually the ALL-category BALCAT SRs; the targeted-subset SRs are core 0.241 (n=58), random 0.203 (n=59), baseline 0.225 (n=138) - the +3.8pp core-random gap is unchanged; (2) random-baseline paired p is 0.027-0.028 in exact/permutation recomputes (vs claimed 0.024) and is marginal after Bonferroni x3 (corrected ~0.083).

verdicts.claim: No arm flattened the tall-object cliff (h>0.21m): in STRAT, tall SR is baseline 0.09 -> core 0.21 (best, CI[0.15,0.30]), random 0.17, and the saturation arm with ALL 610 targeted demos only 0.14 -- 3x more targeted data bought nothing on tall. The tall-vs-mid penalty actually GREW under core (-30pp -> -38pp) because 8-14cm objects gained most (0.48 -> 0.81). Pooled paired interaction over the 4 targeted-selection arms: tall DD +6.8pp, p=0.14 -- modest tall-concentration possible, large flattening (>~15pp) ruled out.
verdicts.reasoning: Independently recomputed from pooled_episodes.csv (own script, own permutation seed). (1) STRAT tall (h>0.21) SR per arm: baseline 0.087 (9/103), core 0.214 (22/103, Wilson CI [0.145,0.302], best arm), random 0.165, saturate 0.143, failretr 0.188, whiten 0.097 — matches claimed 0.09/0.21 CI[0.15,0.30]/0.17/0.14; every arm <=0.214 with n>=103 tall episodes/arm. arms_saturate.json confirms saturate used 610 targeted demos vs core's 200 (3.05x), and saturate's paired tall gain is only +4.9pp (p=0.37), so "3x more targeted data bought nothing on tall" holds. (2) Tall-minus-mid(4-14cm) penalty: baseline -29.5pp -> core -38.1pp (claimed -30 -> -38); 8-14cm bin 0.481 -> 0.815 (claimed 0.48 -> 0.81) — exact. (3) Pooled paired-config tall interaction over the 4 targeted arms (core/failretr/saturate/whiten): 620 pairs (245 tall), DD=+6.83pp, perm p=0.145 (claimed +6.8pp, p=0.14); DD 95% CI [-1.5,+15.1]pp, so "large flattening >~15pp ruled out" matches the CI upper bound. Adversarial checks failed to refute: tall fraction (0.36-0.37) and tall category mix balanced across arms (no composition confound); zero duplicate configs within any STRAT run (per-arm CIs not pseudo-replicated; config repetition is across runs and is exploited by the paired analysis); cliff persists at thresholds 0.18/0.20/0.24 in all arms; paired-on-shared-configs tall gains show random (+15.2pp, p=0.03) matches core (+12.7pp, p=0.03), reinforcing that no targeted arm specifically flattened the cliff. Minor caveats only: the -38pp penalty uses mid=4-14cm while the 0.48->0.81 figure is the 8-14cm sub-bin (mixed definitions, each number individually correct); random's penalty grew even more (-44pp) so penalty growth is not core-specific; each arm is one training run so arm differences include seed noise, but the claim already reports the interaction as non-significant.

verdicts.claim: The rim penalty was untouched by every arm: pooled paired interaction over targeted arms DD=-0.4pp p=1.0 (STRAT, 185 rim pairs); core-baseline rim gain (+11.2pp) equals its center gain (+11.1pp) exactly. In family E the influence arm significantly WORSENED rim relative to center (DD=-19.6pp CI[-38.0,-0.4], paired p=0.054); coverage trended the same way (-16.5pp).
verdicts.reasoning: Every quoted number reproduces EXACTLY under independent recomputation (rim = max(|x_rel|,|y_rel|)>0.65, config-paired across runs): STRAT pooled targeted-arms interaction DD=-0.4pp perm p=1.0000 with 185 rim pairs/620; STRAT core-baseline gain_rim=+11.2pp vs gain_center=+11.1pp; family E influence unpaired DD=-19.6pp boot CI[-38.0,-0.4] with paired perm p=0.0540; coverage DD=-16.5pp. Design integrity checks pass: no pseudo-replication (all 5021 (run,cfg) rows unique), rim labels config-consistent across arms, and the paired tests control run by within-config cross-run differencing with within-arm-stratum permutation. The headline null ("rim penalty untouched by every arm") is robust: no arm in any family shows a positive rim interaction (best +12.5pp p=0.28), and the pooled null holds across rim thresholds 0.50-0.75 (all p>0.16). HOWEVER, the third sub-claim ("influence significantly WORSENED rim") fails adversarial scrutiny: (a) p=0.054>0.05 and it is one of ~15 rim interaction tests (~36+ across weak dims) — it survives no multiple-comparison correction, and the un-highlighted value arm is stronger (paired DD=-28.9pp p=0.027); (b) the effect is threshold-fragile — at cutoffs 0.50/0.55/0.60 the paired DD is -5.6/+1.1/-6.2pp (p=0.69/1.00/0.64), and a continuous rim-distance test gives r=-0.054 p=0.49, i.e. a cutoff-specific spike, not a spatial gradient; (c) the claim pairs the unpaired CI with the paired p (paired DD is actually -25.4pp). Also note the pooled null has MDD~14pp, so "untouched" means no rim-relative shift beyond ~±10-14pp (corroborated by the matching +11.2/+11.1 core gains). Direction and magnitudes all reproduce, but "significantly worsened" is an overstatement of a fragile trend, so PARTIAL rather than CONFIRMED.
verdicts.corrected: The rim penalty was not improved by any arm: pooled paired interaction over the 4 targeted STRAT arms DD=-0.4pp, perm p=1.00 (185 rim pairs/620; MDD ~14pp), robust to rim threshold (0.50-0.75); core-baseline rim gain +11.2pp ~= center gain +11.1pp (uniform lift, not rim-targeted). In family E the influence arm showed a non-robust TREND toward worsening rim relative to center (unpaired DD=-19.6pp CI[-38.0,-0.4]; paired DD=-25.4pp p=0.054, uncorrected, 1 of ~15 rim tests; effect vanishes at thresholds 0.50-0.60 and in a continuous rim-distance test, r=-0.054 p=0.49); coverage trended similarly (-16.5pp, p=0.40 paired), and value was actually the strongest such trend (paired DD=-28.9pp p=0.027, also uncorrected).

result.conclusion: Nothing is permanently lost. The pooled CSV's 15 fields are all the harness ever persisted (analyze_pi0_weakregions.py:197-207) — object instance (mjcf path), start yaw, distractor identities/positions, robot base pose, placement side, camera configs and horizon were never written to any eval artifact — but every one of them is recoverable for PAST evals without re-running any policy, because RoboCasa scene generation is fully deterministic in the env seed (single default_rng(seed) drives layout/style, instance sampling, placement, yaw, base jitter, textures) and each record's seed is base_seed + episode with base seeds known from run logs (0 default, 100000 for the paired arms, 300000 for failstates) or stored exactly in phase1_data/eval_set.json. A seed-replay script (saved to scratchpad) re-instantiates each episode's env, verifies the recorded category/layout/style/obj_xy fingerprint, and extracts the full metadata; mass/friction/scale then come from the named mjcf files, and training demos already carry everything in hdf5 ep_meta/model_file attrs. Re-collection with richer logging is therefore never required for recovery — only the small forward patch (spec in scratchpad) is needed so future evals log these fields directly. Priority for the residual-variance hunt: object instance first, yaw second, distractors third; mass last (76% of failures never touch the object). The one caveat: seed replay assumes unchanged robocasa code/assets since the eval — the fingerprint check in the recovery script detects any violation per episode.
